description: Assignment to document.domain — relaxes same-origin policy; not direct XSS but enables it from sibling subdomains

Element.on<event> = … — assigning a *string* (rather than a function) to a DOM event handler. PortSwigger calls this element.onevent. Pair with a string-literal check at the agent level to reduce noise.

Element.setAttribute("on*"|"href"|"src"|"srcdoc"|"formaction"|...) — setting a dangerous attribute via setAttribute is equivalent to direct property assignment; commonly missed because static analysers focus on direct property assignment
$.prepend(...) — jQuery DOM injection. Also matches DOM Element.prepend() which auto-escapes strings; agent should disambiguate.
$.replaceWith(...) — jQuery DOM injection
$.replaceAll(...) — jQuery DOM injection. Also matches String.prototype.replaceAll — high false-positive rate; consider context.
$.wrap / $.wrapAll / $.wrapInner — accept HTML string; jQuery DOM injection
$.insertBefore / $.insertAfter — jQuery DOM injection
$.animate(...) — historic jQuery DOM XSS sink via the properties argument; low severity in modern jQuery
$.parseHTML(str) — parses HTML and can execute scripts when the output is appended to the DOM
$(location.hash) / $(location.search) — classic PortSwigger jQuery selector sink; older jQuery treats the leading "<" as HTML
jQuery $.attr("href"|"src"|"on*"|...) with an attacker-controlled value — javascript: URLs allowed
AngularJS (1.x) $sce.trustAs* — explicit sanitisation bypass
Angular (2+) DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrust* — explicit sanitisation bypass
Vue.compile(template) — compiles a template string; equivalent to eval for templates
AngularJS $compile(html) — compiles an HTML string against a scope; XSS sink
element.src = … — generic .src assignment. Pair with a check that the element is a

element.text|innerText|textContent = … — when the element is a <script>, this *executes* the assigned string. Otherwise auto-escaped (safe). Agent should check element type. NOTE: very high FP rate; only useful for taint flows that target script elements.
iframe.srcdoc = … — full HTML document injection
<object>.data = url — script equivalent for <object>; very high FP rate (matches React/Vue .data on every component); NOISY — disable by default
Range.createContextualFragment(html) — parses HTML; injecting works
new DOMParser().parseFromString(html, "text/html") — parses HTML in an inert document; scripts do NOT execute on parse, only when nodes are adopted into the live DOM. Low severity by itself.
Node.js vm.runIn* / vm.compileFunction — Node V8 sandbox is *not* a security boundary; equivalent to eval
new vm.Script() / new vm.SourceTextModule() — same reasoning as vm.runIn*
child_process.exec / spawn / fork — command-injection sink when the command string is tainted (exec/execSync are highest risk because they go via /bin/sh -c)
require(<expression>) — dynamic require; if the path is user-controlled it can load arbitrary modules. Look-ahead excludes the safe require("...") string-literal form.
setImmediate("code", ...) — Node-specific; like setTimeout-with-string, executes the string as code
Indirect eval forms: (0, eval)(...), globalThis.eval(...), window.eval(...) — webpack/rollup output uses these; NOT caught by a bare \beval\( regex
execScript(...) — legacy IE; same role as eval. Still appears in old code targeting older IE.
Bare `location = …` (not `location.href`) — navigates the current window. Look-behind avoids matching `*.location =`. javascript: URLs execute.
top|parent|self|opener.location[.href] = … — navigation in an alternate frame
element.href = … — applies to <a>, <area>, <link>, <base>. A javascript: URL on an <a> executes when clicked. Low severity by itself; high when followed by .click()
form.action = … — open redirect on submit. NOTE: high FP rate (Redux actions, GraphQL "action" fields).
window.navigate(url) — legacy IE only; rarely seen in modern code
trustedTypes.createPolicy(name, {createHTML, createScript, createScriptURL}) — a custom policy that returns the input unchanged is effectively no-op. Inspect the policy body for actual sanitisation.
lodash _.merge / _.mergeWith / _.defaultsDeep / _.set / _.setWith — historically prototype-pollution sinks (CVE-2018-3721, CVE-2020-8203 etc.)
jQuery $.extend(true, target, source) — deep mode is a prototype-pollution sink (CVE-2019-11358)
Object.assign({}, untrustedObj) — shallow; only an issue when followed by recursive merge into something else. Low severity standalone.
Object.setPrototypeOf(obj, p) — explicit prototype manipulation; tainted p means full pollution
Reflect.setPrototypeOf(obj, p) — same as Object.setPrototypeOf
Direct write to __proto__ via either bracket or dot access — explicit pollution. High severity, low FP.
var X = window.X || { ... } — DOM-clobbering vulnerable pattern (PortSwigger). The OR-fallback means an HTML-injected element with id=X can replace the value.
document.<CapitalizedName> read — named-property-access pattern; HTML-injected element with that id can shadow built-ins. Very high FP; consider only when paired with HTML injection elsewhere.
document.implementation.createHTMLDocument(...) — parses HTML in inert doc; chains with subsequent adoption to live DOM
setAttribute with a dynamic attribute name — attacker-controlled attribute names are exploitable
